analysis:
Examined the changes. ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift head line 82 adds superviseServingAuthorization() to the capacity tick, after inventory refresh and before writeDaemonState. ProviderLoop+Serve.swift adds noteCoordinatorConnection(connected:false) before the event loop starts (head ~299-300). It also adds noteCoordinatorConnection(connected: event.isConnected) in the connection-control reader on .connected/.disconnected (head 426), before clearConnectionAuthorization/cancelAppAttestShadow. A final noteCoordinatorConnection(connected:false) runs at stream end (head 436).

These calls are additive. The existing authorization invalidation on every connection change remains unchanged (base 423-425, 433-434), so T-053's connection-change revocation is preserved. The new tracking is set on the fast control reader, which matches the T-053/TB-011 ordering rationale: it is synchronous and precedes the next session's challenge.

The implementations of noteCoordinatorConnection, superviseServingAuthorization and event.isConnected are not in the supplied evidence. Integration should verify the following:
(1) superviseServingAuthorization only tightens: it expires or revokes grants on expiry or disconnect. It must never extend, re-grant or restore authorization from cached state, per A-016, T-052, T-053 and T-057.
(2) isConnected maps correctly for .connected vs .disconnected.
(3) The periodic tick, running on the loop actor, cannot race a new connection's grant. For example, a stale connected flag must not let an old grant survive.
(4) Any daemon-state or diagnostics output from supervision does not leak identities (T-058).

The capacity tick runs every heartbeat/2 seconds. If supervision blocks or throws, availability could be affected (A-018), but no evidence of that is visible. No regression is identified from the visible code.
